on script that cron starts at 03:00 every day on their Mac mini `edna`. When it finishes it emails the user a summary. Last week it crashed at startup (an expired token) four nights in a row, before it reached the email step, so no email arrived and nobody noticed until the user went looking. Nothing else alerts on this job today. The user also has a Synology NAS at home that can run Docker containers.

The user writes:
"The nightly sync was dead for four days and I only found out by accident. I won't read logs. I'm thinking we should set up a central log on the Synology, Pieter Levels style, maybe everything in Docker? How should we do this?"

You want to be alerted when `nightly-sync` stops completing, without having to read logs.

I recommend an external heartbeat monitor: the script sends a ping only after a successful sync, and the monitor emails you if that ping hasn’t arrived by 03:00 plus the normal runtime and a small grace period. That catches startup crashes and cron failing to run at all; central logs on the Synology would still need this missing-run detection, so a heartbeat is the smallest fix.
